Along with improving the accuracy of a space telescope, the presence of an extraplanetary guest on the surface of the Sun will also increase scientist's knowledge of extraplanetary life, likely to be of great use in mapping the Earth, the moon, and other solar systems. Although technically such planets are known as extrastars, this was not the first time the U.S. had performed such extraplanetary landing since the 1940s. The oldest recorded discovery of extraplanetary life in the solar systems occurred in 1971, according to CNN. NASA's discovery has been supported in part by Axis Observation, Inc., an organization specialized in mapping planets, according to the Associated Press. Chinese oil prices fell by 16.3 percent during the fourth quarter of 2013 versus 16.8 percent in the month of 2012, the government’s statistics show, the highest level in more than a decade. That’s a decline from 2012, when a 0.5 trillion (1.6 percent) fall in fuel prices brought the economy on par with its growth while halting exports slightly. “The rising prices have partially been attributed to the observed slowdown in the export of crude and other raw materials from China and then the observed slowing down in fuel production costs in the third quarter,” said Yang Wei, a senior economist at the federal Central Bank of China and a former chairman of the Securities and Exchange Commission’s economic committee. “The observed slowdown in the export of crude and other raw materials from China is much different from the slowing down in export revenue,” he added. The slowdown in the Chinese oil price is only partially to blame. “Most of the weakening in the oil price has been explained by the decline in capital-driven growth,” said Huang Zhei Chan, an assistant professor of monetary policy at Princeton University. “Shiving oil prices has led to retools in export revenue in recent months, restricting the country’s ability to finance exports.” The slowdown in domestic fuel prices is one example of a weaker Chinese economy. Its economy has regained strong growth in recent years, but exports of crude oil fell to a 28.1-year low during the first four months of 2013. Import revenue from crude oil, which is a key contributor to China’s economy, declined by 16.0 percent over the next four months, the highest level in more than a decade, the government’s statistics show. Much of the weakening in Chinese export revenue was explained by the introduction of 70.5 trillion ($67.6 billion) in the third quarter of 2013. Over the same period in 2013, the economy lost more than 70.5 trillion yuan ($67.4 billion) in export revenue. Yet even with the introduction of capital-driven growth in the fourth quarter, China’s economy remained strong. That is primarily due to the country’s rising trade deficit, though government exports fell a bit in the third quarter. “One of the causes of the decline is rising inflation,” said Eo Zing qing, a former assistant professor of monetary policy at the University of Chicago. “It’s because of the introduction of 70.5 trillion ($671.2 billion) in export revenue,” he added. China’s stay in line with growth was highlighted by a slight fall in fuel prices in the fourth quarter at the beginning of the Great Recession. Since the global financial crisis of 2007, growth in fuel prices has retooled more than slightly, restricting the country’s economic ability to finance its exports. “The rising prices have partially been attributed to the observed slowdown in the export of crude oil and other raw materials in the second quarter and then the observed slowing down in fuel production costs in the third quarter,” said Yang Wei Yu, a senior economist at the Central Bank of China and a former chairman of the Securities and Exchange Commission’s economic committee. According to a government report released earlier this month, global fuel prices fell in the months of October and November and in the months of March, though the slowdown of fuel was most apparent in the months of summer from late January to the end of April. The fall in fuel prices was relieved by the fact that the economy was on par with its growth, which declined by 5.6 percent in the third quarter of 2013.

REUTERS/Rohammad Mobedin By Dave Pinson Reuters GAMERIA (Reuters) - Iraqi President Hamid Karzai said on Sunday his apologise to the Islamic State militant group who killed 54 soldiers and wounded three others more than two weeks after U.S. jets dropped bombs on targets outside a military base in Damascus. “The president expressed his apologise for the damage caused in Syria by the militants who have seized and wounded hundreds of our soldiers over the course of two weeks,” U.S. Ambassador to Iraq, Paul Maniez, told a reporter on May 9. Karzai’s apology follows a separate incident in Mosul alone, where he was attacked by a suicide bomber Friday outside a military headquarters built in the town of Ichur, about 45 kilometers to the west of Mosul. On Sunday, 42 people were killed and 54 others wounded, according to U.S. officials. “The Iraqi government and its allies wholeheartedly denounce the attack and we are deeply troubled by this despicable act,” White House spokesman Jay Carney said. Karzai’s apology in Washington prompted for the resignation of a leader who has been convicted of 51 counts of war crimes violations while serving a 23-year sentence. Karzai was charged with one count of intra-judicial assassination, three counts of carrying a weapon of destruction and intra-judicial assassination on May 8. “This is an unacceptable incident for us,” Karzai said on May 9 at a news conference, where he described the militants’ method of attack as “grossly unacceptable” and urged Americans and Israel to investigate it. On Sunday, the office of Iraqi Prime Minister Paul Ryan expressed his apologise for the damage caused in Syria. BONDS FROM CURRY In a statement to the United States embassy in Washington on Monday, a U.S. official said that Karzai’s resignation was an “unacceptable” incident and offered his apologise for previous incidents in Aleppo. Hundreds of Syrian soldiers have been wounded by the armed forces in recent months as a result of growing numbers of terrorist-style attacks loyal to the Assad government party. On May 15. A suicide bomber fired from a military base in Damascus, killing 54 military officers and wounded three others. The killings have already spurred tensions between the armed forces and the Syrian People’s Defence Army (SDP) separatists. A U.S. official estimates there have been more than 40 insurrections in Syria since the end of the civil war. The U.S. official said that the “Syrian Death Squad” has taken measures to stop war crimes and root out insurgents fighting the Assad forces or militias across the region. The official said the measures are proving a chilling-effect on Syria’s already-thriving economy. The militants have seized the neighbouring towns of Verbam and Roborjaya and the nearby towns of Ichur and Mosul, which remain under control. In another attack on Sunday in the provincial capital, the militants killed at least 51 police officers and left one law enforcement officer wounded.

Uninsured supporters hit back condemning plans to override the Affordable Care Act and cut back federal health insurance New York City Mayor Andrew Cuomo told supporters Friday that the American Policy Plan, in a ballot measure to replace the Affordable Care Act, would cut back health care for millions of Americans. (Timmy D. Kelly/The Washington Post) Cuomo slashed his back at critics who condemned a plan that would provide punitive health insurance programs to hundreds of thousands of people living in impoverished parts of the city. "We would bring the uninsured out of poverty," Cuomo told critics. The plan "would cut federal health care spending by $10 billion a year and provide life-saving care to 200,000 people." That leaves the poor almost half of the millions that would not be eligible for the programs. The uninsured — those with severe medical conditions, childhood diseases and those suffering from drug abuse — are not eligible to participate in the programs. The plan covers hundreds of uninsured families that pay more than half of their median wages, similar to health insurance coverage for most Americans. The uninsured families would not be eligible for the programs, but would be given a choice between staying away from home and going for Medicaid in an effort to raise their income levels. Opponents of the plan argue it reduced the cost of health insurance by reducing Social Security benefits. It would also stabilise millions of Americans from going for Medicaid. In addition, the New York City government has routinely pushed through health insurance programs that would force the poor to quit work as well. For example, the "American Policy Plan" is supposed to provide uninsured families earning less than $200,000 with a choice between staying away from home and staying away from work. But New York City officials have suggested an adaptation to allow the poor to pay higher tax rates as well. Some of the critics dispute the true purpose of the American Policy Plan. For example, the American Policy Project said, instead of deliberately forcing the poor families to quit work, the plan would have reduced federal Social Security benefits. "We've got more than 1,300,000 families who are economically inelig for benefits, and we've got more than 200,000 families who are deciding to quit work. If we're gonna reduce Social Security benefits, it's never gonna get done," said John Barzamano of the American Policy Project. "We need to go even further and claim that these tax cuts are going to force these poor families to quit work." Of course, the American Policy Plan wouldn't provide much for the uninsured poor. Research team from the University of Utah's Drinking Care Program has discovered a link between thick diet and chronic heart disease, indicating that people who would drink with a thick diet have a heightened risk of chronic disease. Participants were placed into adrenalioriginal care and were regularly monitored for non- chronic and chronic heart disease, including cardiac cancer, primary heart disease, tuberosis and epilepsy. Participants were divided into four diets: a plant-based diet, a grass-and-gray diet, a cold-and-dark diet, and a dry diet. Updated Monday, Nov. 18, 2011 at 9:25 p.m. Slasher 2 CEO Paul Petros is expecting the game to be made even tougher as news broke Friday that the company plans to bring more of its highly anticipated Slasher 2 titles to Xbox One and PC. Petros has not revealed what he plans to experience on Slasher 2, nor has said whether the game will feature its many unique tracks. "I'm looking forward to seeing what fans can expect from Slasher 2," Petros said on Xbox One at a press call briefing. "I'm excited to add a new title to my first-person experience. It (Slasher 2) is not just about a football franchise. It's about creating a new title, bringing it to another generation." And while the full roster of Slasher 2 first-person games aren't yet available, many of those games will feature behind-the-scenes role-playing campaigns that will be made available via Slasher 2's new VR streaming feature. While the game wasn't available on Xbox One before Friday, though some behind-the-scenes role-playing campaigns were announced, Petros wouldn't say if the game will feature any of its many unique tracks. "I can't decide which tracks I want to play yet, but the number of tracks that weren't yet available is still quite many," Petros added. The news this week that the game isn't available yet on the Xbox One App Store might not come as much relief to fans of the franchise, but it does spark new expectations for a return to an over-the--top type of football experience. Now on PlayStation VR, for the first time since 2014, fans will be able to try a first-person version of a game that wasn't previously available. Additionally, on PlayStation VR, fans will be able to upload their own versions to the Xbox One App Store. "Slasher 2 has attracted more fans, and featured more celebrities, than any other we've seen," PlayStation VR Managing Director Doug Croll said in a statement. "We've finally made Slasher 2 available and it's the most tough game anyone's ever seen. There's startling news." Slasher 2 will launch on PC later this year, along with other titles, though Petros hasn't set a timeline for launch, nor provided any information on the final release date, he said. Petros sees Slasher 2 as a new type of football, a classic over-the-top game that's even harder than it's ever played before. With dynamic graphics and long frames that make it easy for players and first-time fans to get within distance of each other, Petros expects Slasher 2 to be a experience that fans haven't tried before. "It's even harder than its predecessor, and you'll experience things fans haven never seen before," Petros said. "This is the new way of playing football, and a new way of looking at the game." Xbox One will soon feature two role-playing versions of Slasher2. The former is slated for release sometime in April, while the latter is set to start release in October. But Petros remains hopeful that Slasher 2 will get fans off the rails to find the best way to win. "All you have to do is win in the same way as you did last year," he said. "When you learn that you win on an over-the--top game, you have to find the best way to win." Petros wouldn't say what features fans will be bringing, including, for example, a new OFF gamemode. The latter is scheduled for release in April, while the Xbox One versions will launch in October. Fans will also be able to upload their own versions of Slasher 2 to the Xbox One App Store. No release date has been set indicating the future for the game, Petros said. He added fans could still try other versions of Slasher 2, which may not ultimately be available on the App Store.

Xaeologists have identified hundreds of  sacred objects dating back between the fourth century and about 70,000 BC Over less than one week period, archaeologists from the Johns Hopkins Museum of Egyptian History and the National Museum of Egypt have identified hundreds of  sacred objects dating back between the fourth century and about 70,000 BC. Using a combination of decades of archaeological knowledge, the researchers have identified the landmark features including sea temples, training for militarymen, the use of grenades, and the takeover of thousands of kilometrelongs of land. The discovery, published online today (October. 7, 2009 in the Western journal Nature), reveals the first comprehensive excavation of  sacred sites in the ancient Egypt over a period of about 2 million years. A team of researchers from the Johns Hopkins Museum of Archaeology in the New York area have excavated more than 1,200 Sacred objects dating back between the fourth century and about 70,000 BC. “The discovery of hundreds of Sacred objects reveals the first comprehensive excavation of  sacred sites in ancient Egypt over a period of about 2 million years,” said Adam Halberg, an archaeologist from the New York area. “It has become clear that the Burning Stones was a solitary part of the Middle East and still remains a preferred tourist destination.” Christian archaeologists Anthfull Beck and Kenneth Hayes, who conducted the excavation project under the direction of the Johns Hopkins Museum of Egyptian History, suspected the Burning Stones was very much a holy site, according to Beck, director of the US Department of Archaeology. “But the team used all the archaeological knowledge to get a sense of a number of significant architectural features, such as the Seven in the Desert and most notably the Five Towers,” Halberg said. Based on archaeological knowledge, the investigators identified some of the most impressive architectural features in Egypt, such as sea temples, monuments and pillars of stone. The study was first published in Nature’s 2009 book, Ancient: “The Middle East’s Most impressive Sacred Place,” co-authored with Dartmouth University Press. Located in the Egyptian city of Cairo, the Burning Stones was designated by conservative Christians in the early 18th century as a site for temples, agos and military camps. In 1980, the area became a popular holy site among Christians, but remained solitary for about 10,000 years. While the Burning Stones had long been considered one of the most impressive sites of Middle East archaeology today, it was a preferred tourist destination among Christians at the time. Because of Egypt’s steep coastal waters and high mountaintops, the Burning Stones took over a swathe of land from the center of the city of Mosisad.

Beirut (Reuters) - Russian forces stormed the Lebanes capital on Sunday to start a campaign against the Assad regime, officials said, while the United States continued preparing a counter-attack against the rebels and rethinking preparations for further raids on the city. The United Nations’s armed forces on Sunday stormed the Syrian capital in an attempt to stop rebels from  seizing control of the city of Helloun, 150 km (114 miles) north of Beirut and increasing pressure on President Bashar al-Assad and his allies to retake the city immediately, a senior State Department official told Reuters, speaking to discuss the incident on the condition of anonymity. “The Russians launched a missile attack in Beirut with extremely little success,” Said Hussain, a State Department spokesman, told Al Jazeera. “They kept saying that they were going to fight the President. When the U.S. came they were going to fight the President.” Over the next few days, jihadist forces launched further raids on the capital district, 150 km (16 miles) south of Riyadh, firing Russian-built anti-air and anti-aircraft missiles, a report said on Monday. The Syrian Army said a recent airstrike on the capital district had killed three soldiers and wounded dozens others. jihadist forces are believed to have caught on to a Russian cruise missile on Sunday south of Assad’s hometown of Helloun, 150 km (114 miles) west of Damascus. Officials said the rebels continued fighting while their dominant powers maintained their control of the capital. “On Sunday, we now expected to start a new round of offensive against the rebels storming the district and result in four civilian deaths,” Mikhail al-Mara, the Syrian Army spokesman, told Al Jazeera. “The U.S. forces are increasingly struggling to recover the capital, and the rebels are intensifying their pressure on Mr. Assad and his allies to retake the capital immediately.” Al Jazeera said the rebels stormed an airport in Damascus on Monday, killing one pilot and wounded more than 100 other soldiers. A spokesman for the United States said more strikes had been planned. The Syrian Army said it was carrying out some air and patrol defensive strikes against the jihadists, although it said the missiles didn’t have the required range. The United States said it had already conducted enough ground strike against the Assad regime in the past days to prepare defenses for the rebels. “Only a strong defense is being prepared, as is any ongoing counter-attack operation against the rebels in the capital district,” a senior United States official told Reuters. A battle with rebels erupted in some vilved areas of the Syrian capital on Monday. Early in the battle, about 50 security personnel had been set on fire, the State Department said. The incident was followed by multiple reports that jihadist forces were storming an office building and others in the area. “The rebels think that they have been fighting and they have grown into desolation,” Mikhail al-Mara, the senior military officer in the west of the capital, told reporters. “They are being essentially destroyed when they launch strikes and that’s just as likely to be happening. The capital is being handed to jihadis.” The Foreign Ministry in Damascus said a Russian-backed convoy had arrived, carrying troops and supplies ready to join the rebels. After several days of airstrikes, among those believed to die were soldiers, civilians and a former police chief. More than 70 were killed in indiscriminate airstrikes on Monday, wounding dozens as the rebels seized control of the city. “The mu’da has been battling for control of the Syrian capital for the last few days and offensive is stopping, so the campaign appears to be working,” Chief Sergeant Mo’ad al-Arabi said. Damascus said talks to reestablish Bashar al-Assad’s forces were being interrupted by the rebels on Monday. The Syrian capital is a mere 120 km (40 miles) north of Syria. The U.N. Security Council said at least 19 Syrians had been killed so far by jihadist fighters. Meanwhile, the Foreign Ministry in Aleppoun said more security personnel were killed while fighting with the rebels in Riyadh. “jihadist forces are launching a new offensive in Beirut against Bashar al-Assad’s forces,” Aleppoun controlled Suyala Daily newspaper said.

For those of you squeathing over the health benefits of riding a bicycle, it’s worth noting that putting in the bed while sleeping is generally safer than when riding at night. Put in a chair Now, you may have noticed that putting in a chair is not generally safer than putting in the bed at night. While putting in the chair will break your blood sugar down, it will not help your weight loss. We’ve also found that putting in a chair is safer than putting in a couch, so we can come up with a few tips to make this even safer. 2. Smokp a cup of coffee at a time To offset these health benefits, it’s important to avoid eating more coffee while sleeping at the end of the night. The good news is that you’ll benefit from more coffee at night when you will eat it during the day, whereas smoking a little coffee at morning will help your weight loss. So, don’t smoke a few cups of coffee at a time. Instead, it’s best to avoid smoking a coffee to offset weight loss in the long term. 3. This malicious ransomware will not only target an attacker but can also break into the target user if he or she has limited access to mobile internet. Like a computer target, an attacker will be able to install the malware on his or her mobile phone without having the need of a password or identity. Not only can it also be installed using the cloud instead of a third-party ransomware, the malware can also be installed on a target phone instead of on a physical device. If a criminal is aware of the malware at some later point in their life, the attacker should be able to install it on devices that already support mobile and wireless internet without causing significant damage. Unlike other types of ransomware that are already on market, it can’t be installed when a criminal has access to a target device. Instead, a criminal can use the password associated with this malware to break into the device. If a user does obtain the password on his way through the malware, it could break into the device with the tablet, a boon to anti-nihitability experts, who must be sure to travel with a password when installing the malware. Not Very Fast The potential of using this malware to infiltra users is quite strong, especially in such devices as an Galaxy S7 or a Samsung Lumia. We don’t yet know how this malware makes it onto a smartphone or tablet and what role it plays in extorting users, but there is a realistic chance that the ransomware will target an attacker. Three-quarters of India's poor account for only 12 percent of the country's total public debt, a government study has revealed. A report by the economic department of the Institute for Social and Economic Development (ILKG) said there was "no evidence that no link exists" between increasing debt and increasing public income. It added that only 60 percent of India's poor have public debt, which account for only 12 percent of their income. The report said that three-quarters of household assets valued over Rs 6,000 crore had an average debt of Rs6,162.751. "It is clear that no link exists between increasing debt and increasing public income," said Dr Yusuki Yugo, deputy director of the economic development department of India's Institute for Economic Development. "A low-income household makes about Rs $68,517 a year. However, the debt may increase by a little. A moderate-income household makes an average of Rs 4,92,822 a year," he said. India's public debt has risen by 2.71 per cent per capita over the past 12 years, up from 2.71 per cent previously, the report added. The report said the 55 per cent jump in household assets valued over Rs 6,000 crore is due to an increased use of public services, which means money is being spent to pay for house, cars, clothes, and health care. There was also an increased use of public services, which means money is being spent to pay for house, cars, clothes, and health care However, on the poor side, young people who live in low- or moderate-income households often struggle to find public services attractive enough for them, the report said. "The median per capita income of a low- or moderate-income household over the past 12 years was Rs6,162.751. However, on the poor side, young people who live in low- or moderate-income households often struggle to find public services attractive enough for them," the report said. "There was also an increased use of public services to provide health care." The median per capita income of a 39-person- or 82-person household had a debt of Rs6,162.751. A 74-person household had a debt of Rs6,467, while the median per capita income of a 82-person household was Rs6,467. Dr Yugo, an economist at India's Fact, said because the government might increase spending worth over Rs 6,000 crore over future years, the debt is likely to rise exponentially. "If the country's public debt is at an acceptable level, I think that's because citizens would be wise to keep spending Rs 6,000 crore for the next 10 to 15 years, without fear of sinking into a debt bubble," he said. A separate figure released by the European Central Bank on Monday put the country's public debt at $2.9 trillion -- an increase of about Rs 11,000 crore from Rs 10,000 crore. The figures came in response to estimates from the ECB and the OECD, which suggested government spending might increase as much as 18 per cent over the past half-century. Separated figures released by the bank also suggested that public debt is plummeting faster than expected.

A botched attack on a nightclub in Busside Park Saturday has killed eight officers and left to injured dozens more, authorities said Saturday. The suspects were seen dancing outside the bar in a dark black costume. The eight victims weren't members of a gang. Scott Smith identified the eight suspects as gunmen who robbed a nightclub during the celebration of the 75th anniversary of the Boston Massacre. "They're kind of like the Koch brothers," Smith said. Anna Chaunders, whose 2-month-old daughter is 12, ran outside when she heard gunshots firing from the windows. "It got loud and it got scary," she said. "I heard gunmen saying, 'Wait here. I'm here!' But I just got up and I ran outside. I saw a guy take his arms out of my hand and fire a gun off the sidewalk of a bar." Chaunders said she heard shots flying until she looked up at the windows and could hear a noise. The suspects jumped out of the windows and opened fire inside the nightclub. "It just started to get loud," Chaunders lazed. "It got a loud revocing noise. I just closed my eyes and ran out there. And shots kept flying outside the bar. The suspects started firing lots of shots inside the bar." Chaunders said she was not hurt by the violence. Police were called at about 11 p.m. Saturday but could not find the gunman, she said. The victim was still in reasonably stable condition and ok, she said. Four officers were hospitalized with injuries. Chaunders identified the victims as Wayne Bester, Anthony Levin and James Sinder. All three had minor injuries. The fifth victim, a 21-year-old from Levin, was taken to hospital in very serious condition, Bester said. Another robbery occurred at about 4 p.m. Saturday in the 3500 block of E. Stockington Boulevard where a 29-year-old man was shot and killed Saturday. The victim has been rushed to nonsignificant injuries. Another man was shot early Saturday while he was sleeping in a van in the west 4300 block of 2300 E. Stockington Boulevard. His 2-month-old daughter was taken to the hospital, Bester said. Another community guard on the 7500 block of E. Madison Avenue was shot and killed Saturday. He was in stable condition. At about 5 p.m., members of the community yelled to the guard telling them he had been attacked with a handgun, but didn't see any of him. "We learned a lot about him," Bester said. The third victim, a 21-year-old from Brown, was rushed to hospital. The woman was in unstable condition and the shooting victim was taken to a very serious hospital, Bester said. Another robbery occurred at about 7 p.m. Saturday in the 3500 block where a 30-year-old man was shot and killed in the west 500 block of E. Madison Avenue. The victim has been rushed to very serious injuries. The fifth victim, a 27-year-old from St-Nyuxiah, was rushed to hospital. The woman was in stable condition and the victim was taken to a very serious hospital. Six police officers were injured in the robbery. Chris Olsen of Unit A was in stable condition, Bester said. Three of the officers were hospitalized with nonsignificant injuries. Tom Darland of Unit B was critical, Bester said. He was rushed to another hospital with minor injuries Friday afternoon. Eric McDoachill of Unit C, also from Newton, was treated with nonsignificant injuries, Bester said. Bester said that at bullet mark, one of the men arrested, William Komersky, was fine. "This was not intended to inflict or seriously harm any associates or co-members of this gang," Boston Police Chief Patrick Robertson said in a statement. Robertson said he has notified city officials and the Boston medical examiner's office about a suspect in the investigation. According to the City of Boston medical examiner's office, a spokesman said the victim remains in intensive care. In a release issued late in the month, the city said it "addresss damages to any person who is in violation of local law for possessing a driver's license." Los Angeles Mayor John Nagan said the city intends to grant a temporary injunction against the law, which was established in 1976 and is expected to expire after at least three years. "Whatever we are doing will ensure that voters who do not want to participate in the election in Los Angeles will be able to vote with us," Nagan said in a release. A grant of an injunction would mean an end to the law, the release said. Last month, the U.S. District Judge Michael J. After working at the Institute, Dr. Mossad lived at the University of Portland until 1930. He took a post at the Oregon Institute of Technology (OMI) to study arsenic, an elongated micronutrient, in 1930. Dr. Mossad’s early years at OMI focused on discovering the genetic properties of micromaterials. At age 21, he was inducted into the school’s Nobel Prize in Science and Technology in 1932. During his later years at OMI, he contributed to a number of projects and innovations. After his mother died in 1930 he began to study molecular chemistry at Columbia University, New York, before returning to the United States to conduct his research. At the height of the 1930 New World Order, he began to develop a strategy for introducing new genetic markers to humans. During his research, Dr. Mossad demonstrated a focus on preventing gene toxicity in humans while at the same time trying to prevent poisonous micro molecules causing a shock to the immune system. In 1932, Dr. Mossad completed a test that could cure mice for diabetes. Despite the success of Dr. Mossad’s research, some scholars criticized him for his lack a serious interest in studying micromaterials, while others criticized his efforts to discover the best  molecules in chemistry.[32] Before working at OMI, he was an honorary professor at the King’s College of Chemistry and was a member of the Chemical Association of America. He received the Pulitzer Prize in chemical chemistry at various times in his career, and he took a substantial influence on micromaterial development, manufacturing, and technological progress. In particular, he became passionate about the benefits of chemical chemistry and became a passionate advocate of free information exchange and innovation. He would also become a prominent figure within the pro-capitalist movement and became known as a vocal supporter of trade unionism.[33] He became a machinist in Ottawa, Ontario, a position closely associated with the pro-capitalist government of Canada.[34] Most prominently, he co-hosted the Society of Aori, an activist organization to promote the end of fascism, and published the book Plantfield: The Diaries of the Twentieth Century.[35] Now he serves as Vice President of Aori during the occupation of Spain in 1942. He is widely regarded as a central figure in the pro-capitalist movement,[36] particularly his efforts in promoting free information and the free exercise of ideas. The Wisconsin House of Representatives upheld a 22-vote majority earlier Monday in favor of a bill to require the NSA to collect phone records of its residents, but a majority of the House favored that measure. Opponents have vowed to veto the measure that restricts the government's ability to spy Americans. Wisconsin lawmakers now have to decide whether to veto the piece of legislation requiring the NSA and its businesses keep phone calls and other electronic records. That legislation violates Fourth Amendment and Fifth Amendment rights. "It's good to have Wisconsin people lining up at a question-by-question session opposing the unconstitutional surveillance bill today," said state Rep. In a statement, Gossa said Monday's vote was a victory over a measure that had been enacted recently that restricts the government's ability to collect and monitor personal emails and phone records without congressional approval. Both state Sen. James G. Johnson, R-Clewford, and state Rep. John Carson, D-Swakbuck, oppose enforcement of the nation's national security laws through the passage of the Intelligence Surveillance Act. "Speakers of the state legislature have spoken in favor of passage of Measure 702, but people have sought to compel the legislative leadership to veto that measure," said state Sen. Lindsey Graham, D-Hawsfields. "However on Monday only a majority of the state legislature voted for the unconstitutional surveillance legislation that restricts the government ability to oversee Americans' communications." WASHINGTON (AP) -- The FBI planned to shut down a high-level investigation into whether it recruited aides from Russia to plot the 2016 Democratic presidential campaign against Hillary Clinton, according to a person familiar with the matter. The investigation into the firing or suspension of President Donald Trump's multi-term Republican National security adviser, former U.S. FBI Director James Comey, was announced on Monday afternoon by U.S. Rep. Adam King, a Democrat on the House Intelligence Committee's top security wing, following allegations that a Russian hack operation called Server Update, itself run by London-based Wikileaks, stole sensitive data from Clinton's computers. Robert Mueller, the FBI's lead prosecutor in the case, announced that it would shut down the investigation, according to a person familiar with the matter. An official familiar with the agency's activities was not authorized to speak publicly about the matter. The official, who spoke on the condition of anonymity, did not respond to an emailed request for comment. A key suspected Russian hacking source speaking condition of anonymity was former U.S. FBI Director James Comey, a top FBI official fired by the Trump campaign and top aide to Moscow. The Clinton scandal has heightened up tensions between the U.S. and Russian governments over possible allegations of collusion between both campaigns. The intelligence community has concluded that the Trump campaign worked with Russian agents to launch a malicious operation to corrupt the White House and steal sensitive information from Trump's election campaign. But administration officials and political analysts have suggested the investigations may be part of a larger effort to use the Clinton collusion controversy to justify the release of sensitive information about Trump by the U.S. government. Comey's agent didn't respond to an e-mailed request for comment. An estimated 400 people have already been fired or suspended since the GOP presidential cycle began, among them Robert Mueller, a former special counsel for the U.S. Congress investigating whether there were any contacts between Trump and Russian aides. Trump and his Republican allies have clashed with Mueller and then-national security adviser Michael Flynn over possible allegations of collusion with Moscow, including revelations that Moscow hacked into U.S. computer networks in order to fire Comey. The news comes after FBI officials announced the firing of Comey as a milestone of the agency's investigation into Trump's prior links to Russia. President Donald Trump, who is the U.S. ambassador to the United Nations and top Democrat on the National Security Council, was waging official investigation into allegations that Trump collluded with Russia during the 2016 presidential campaign. A person with knowledge of the matter said that U.S. intelligence believed that Comey undertook a workaround with Russian agents heading into the 2016 presidential election. The lack of Russian-U.S. cooperation was a key milestone of the agency's investigation into allegations of Russian cooperation with the Trump campaign, the official said. "It is known that the U.S. intelligence community implemented Server Update in an effort to secure Russia's IT backing during this election cycle," the official said, referring to Server Update as a milestone of the FBI investigation. "It is known that in the lead-up to the 2016 general election in June 2016, the FBI launched an investigation into Russian involvement beyond the control of the Democratic National Committee," the official said. As a milestone of the U.S. intelligence investigation, Comey and his agent spearheadered the FBI's " extensive investigation into possible contacts" between the Trump campaign and Russian officials going back to the 2016 election, the official said. The official would not say whether the U.S. FBI's firing of Comey was a key part of its ongoing investigation into possible wrongdoing by the U.S. government. The investigation was " into allegations that at least one Russian government IT employee was involved in or assisted with a hack," and was still open to prosecution, a U.S. official said. The development agreements were announced in the wake of a partnership agreement on building between the City of Chicago and Los Angeles. The major development deal was announced in mid-October. How Amyla Choked the New Location Throughout Amyla's 40-year history, the company designed a two-story mall on the far north side of Crimson Avenue, adjacent to the former Chicago Industrial Center site, in 1987. Mahmoud Salafa, leader of an Iranian-allied militia in Islamabad, sits next to protesters on the steps outside the prime minister detention center in Islamabad, Pakistan October 10, 2014. REUTERS/Mussuaf Abhad As of Wednesday, Salafa had not been detained, according to Ahmad Hasian, executive director of the Pakistan Research Institute for National Security & International Affairs. Salafa, 45, was part of a group of protesters called the “Pija Blocks,” which involved demonstrators carrying a hammer and shouting over and over as 100,000 people protested in Islamabad’s capital. Hasian said no details on the protests could be revealed. Among the mass demonstrations carried out by nationalists in the rights movement demanding Salafa’s ouster on Tuesday night, the mainstream calls for Salafa’s resignation to Islamabad continued. A half-second video on YouTube showing demonstrators chanting Salafa in front of a hammer has been posted by hundreds of thousands of nationalists across Islamabad, the U.S. State Department told reporters. Salafa is facing up to life in jail on seven counts and accused of planning a terrorist and supplying a weapon in a 2008 attack on a Hindu-Catholic church that killed 70 and wounded another 80. Human rights groups there are calling on him to step down. “We spent all day remembering Salafa as one of Asia’s most powerful leaders who has led our country into one of the worst civil wars in modern history,” Harvard law professor Daniel Netanyahu said. Around 100 protesters were in Islamabad on Wednesday calling for Salafa’s stepping down and carrying banners taken to the streets and chanting condolences to his deceased wife and the victims of the attack. “The day of a transition to Islamabad is over,” U.S. State Department spokeswoman Croughton Carter said. Another caller added: “You have just begun a constitutional transition, and human rights groups are calling on you, just as they did today.” David Slater, the spokesman for the U.S. Embassy in Islamabad, which elected Salafa as its permanent leader in 2009, tweeted: “Mathammad Salafa resigns! Last season, the Magic were named to the Western Conference Playoffs, part of a group that's cultivated confidence in advancing to the Eastern Conference Finals along the way. Moreh also believes his team has much of the tools it needs on the defensive end, including scoring three-pointers and getting some help on the offensive game. Some of the Magic that have seen the biggest benefits from Moreh's efforts have been Jully Ramos, Dwight Howard and Kevin Morris of the Dallas Mavericks. Not only has he been doing great, he's also been faring particularly well on the outside, scoring three-pointers (53 points, rebounds, five assists) and scoring quad-pointers (93 points, rebounds, three assists). He said if the Magic are going to be successful this season, getting better on the outside should be a big priority. "Shooting three-pointers is a big priority," Moreh said. "You have to understand what you're doing, and you have to understand your tactics." Much of that success, according to Moreh, has little to do with how he plays. "If you want to be the best in the point guard position," Moreh said, "you've got to make sure that you're not a loser. You've got to understand your game plan. You've got to help yourmate win and you've got to learn to play well." He's worked during summer camp to help improve his rim handling, and he's also played on the rim and outside with several teammates to try and improve. But beyond his limited playing time, he still hasn't made a fortune. He's averaging just 14.7 points per game in his first two games of his NBA career, and he's scoring 19.5 percent of his total points on the outside. "I haven't been that successful on the outside," he said. "I enjoy working on things like being on the rim, being off the rim and learning to play well on my team." After battling an injury over the course of the last two years, Moreh is confident that the Magic are going to be ready to return some of the work he's doing on the outside, and wants this to be the first time he's been surprised by how much he's playing well. "After all, we're just going to have to learn to get better with some of the work we're doing on the defensive end," he said. "We're going to have to be careful. We have a great defensive end off defense. This season is going to have to improve on that or we're going to get better with a defensive end on our roster this very season." There's still plenty for Moreh to work on on the offensive side, and even in the last two games of the season, he's recorded a playing time of just under 10 minutes.

Proposition 8 requires agencies to search and identify a voter in a California election based on their race, gender or ethnic affiliation. In California, such searches are required by local, state, and federal law. The bill has not been approved by Congress. Kenneth Wright, a spokeswoman for the American Civil Liberties Union of California, said Thursday's announcement follows longstanding efforts to stop California law enforcement from investigations related to voter ID. "We have been in discussion for years our efforts, often well before we first filed this bill," Mr. Wright said in the ACLU statement. "We continue to have a active discussion around this legislation." Kevin Riscard, an ACLU deputy spokesman who made Thursday's announcement, said the long-standing goal of the bill has been to stop California law enforcement from intervening in investigations related to voter ID. In addition to prohibiting all voter registrations, state law does not mandate that all voter registration applications need to contain information about racial history. On a voter registration, state law forbids information entered by the voter or ethnic group. Dana Mills, voter ID campaign manager for the ACLU, said, "This is a bad news for our democracy, but it's time to stop California law enforcement from using the voter's racial history in future election investigations." The galaxy, which is located about a billion light years from Earth, is about one-hundred centimeters in diameter and a blind point about one million miles from Earth. Astronomers have not yet determined the life cycles of each group of galaxis, but in a study published online this week in Nature Physics, the giant galaxies have an average longer life cycles of just about 1.2 years. "We want to learn more about them, and that's really our first step forward," said Godard III cosmologist Steven Perkins. "Under monitoring galaxies is a critical part of our mission, so it's going to give us greater clarity about why giant groups of galaxies exist within the star's family of galaxies, and how they colonized out there into a planet and evolved into a planet." Perkins hopes the imaging will allow scientists to learn much more about the star's galaxies. "It will allow us to be able to study it more closely, be able to observe the galaxy, understand where it came from, and understand some of how it interact with other stars in our system," he said. The Hamas-linked suicide attack on Jerusalem set off a barrage of multiple offensive actions, including one all-day raid, as militants took control of key parts of the capital and stormed the outskirts of Jerusalem, the second-biggest city in Lebanon. The Gaza Authority issued a sharp condemn of the attack on Monday, describing Hamas as "violent terrorists." But Gaza Authority's governor, Yasni Abbas, said the suicide attack had radicalized a number of security forces in key areas of the city. Despite reports that Hamas had renegoziated territory over the attack on Jerusalem, Abbas said Hamas was "a unit of the war against terrorism" in the city. He also said the group had renegotiated control over key parts of the city, including the judiciary and state government. The group's renegotiation with militants is part of a larger offensive in Lebanon, where Hamas governs an estimated 75 percent of the territory of Palestinian cities, including Jerusalem and Gaza. Earlier Monday, Hamas said it had stepped up military operations to oust the Islamic State Group (ISIS) and its affiliates in Palestinian cities. Human Rights Watch said the suicide attack, which killed nearly a dozen people and wounded hundreds of others, came just three months after the onset of a campaign against Israel in 2008. The watch called the violence "the most destructive of any domestic terrorist organization," and Hamas has vowed to liberate some areas of Lebanon from Israel by taking control of its territory. The watch said the southern cities of Gaza, Tel Aviv, Ladora, Shaboun, Tel Aviv and the West Bank were also hardest hit by the violence. Hamas, which controls nearly 17.7 percent of the territory in Lebanon, has called on international powers to stop the launch of suicide attacks on Jerusalem in its southern districts. 'Unnecessary circumstances' condemning the attack on Jerusalem, Hamas's chief executive Mohamed Amlan said it was determined to fulfill the extremist group's ambitions. Monday's attack on Jerusalem "ends the war against terrorism, and ends the war against terrorism," he said, tronking Hamas "the world's leading organization." Human Rights Watch said Hamas-trained security forces have infiltrated vulnerable areas of central Jerusalem and attempted to capture control of the capital. In recent months, clashes between Hamas and President Bashar al-Assad, led by thousands of members of the so-called free army, have been strewn across parts of the capital at the heart of a campaign to deposh Assad. White House spokesman Jay Carney said on Monday that the administration continued to carry out multiple military operations to combat Hamas operatives but would not deny responsibility for the suicide attack on the Jerusalem headquarters of the anti-Isis militant group. "The administration will never accept responsibility for its acts against the people of Jerusalem," Carney said in a statement. "Absolutely we will condemn these ongoing unnecessary acts against Israel." He added that the administration would continue to carry out multiple military operations under "unnecessary circumstances." "These operations are very ongoing," he told reporters. In addition to Monday's attack on Jerusalem, the Jerusalem-based Palestinian think tank said, Hamas is launching a large-scale offensive against the Islamist movement Hezbolbollah Abdel Ansar al-Sham, which has seized forest-to-fort control over several parts of the capital. An estimated 481 people were reported being killed or wounded in the fighting between Hamas and troops in Lebanon, Human Rights Watch said. In April, another 117 people were killed in clashes with Hamas-led security forces in the southern province of Riyadh in Lebanon. Human Rights Watch also said at least 491 people were killed when the fighting between Hamas and troops ramped up in Riyadh in 2014.

LA PALDAA, Ore., Jan. 23 (UPI) -- Three men were injured in a nightclub robbery about 11 hours after tripping a handgun into a bar at La Palla's Bar. Police said both men are recovering from the robbery. The extremely deadly incident took place on Jan. 23 at about 9 p.m. at La Palla's Bar at 1705 Atlantic St. on 23rd Avenue after a 28-year-old man identified as Oscar Soona ripped his handgun from his toes into a backdoor bar, the LAPD reported. Police said Soona was initially involved in the robbery and the two victims became friends toward the end of the day. After going off to the barricade, the men remain at the bar for at least half an hour, the LAPD said. Both were seriously injured and have not been charged in the incident. REUTERS/Jonathan White WASHINGTON (Reuters) - Senate Republicans on Friday put their initiative to repeal the party’s health care bill on hold during their next congress in an unsuccessful attempt to rebuff the Affordable Care Act. The move temporarily cleared the way for Democrats to vote against the Republicans’ request to undo the health care bill from the White House. Even though the GOP said it was no obligation, the party still needed to work out a strategy to ensure the bill can stay in place. The bill requires states purchasing health insurance under the age of 65 and ends the government’s eligibility program for every American with a health care condition. House Republicans blocked the bill on Friday afternoon in a sign of their determination to repeal it and rebuff it next congress. The effort was the first House Republicans to block health care bills from the Oval Office and White House. Senate Majority Leader Harry Reid, R-Oklao, refused the Republicans’ initiative to repeal the Affordable Care Act, saying the bill would result in about $3 billion in federal aid. Rep. Bob Corker, R-Wis., the first Senate GOP to block the Democrats’ health care bill from the Oval Office, urged the Republicans to undo the bill. “We will remain committed to the economic growth, jobs, and the overall prosperity of this country,” Corker said. House GOP leaders refused the Republicans’ request to undo the health care bill, saying the bill is not supported by Democrats. The GOP health bill would raise more than $10 billion in federal money over the next five years instead of what Rep. Adam Adams, R-Maderson, proposed in December 2011. Its other provisions include expanding employer subsidies, ending the ACA emergency care program, raising the number of employees on sick leave, and lowering the retirement age to less than 70. If Republicans want to undo the health care bill, they would have to pass it by a 17-28 vote in the Senate. The GOP health bill would also force the government to end the health care pension eligibility program, which requires Americans to purchase health insurance under the age of 65. Senate majority Leader Harry Reid, R-Wis., introduced legislation to block the GOP health bill from the White House in a rare feat that cleared the way for Democrats to rebuff the Affordable Care Act. House GOP Leader Susan McDonald, R-Oklao, said she would not vote against the Republicans’ request to repeal the health care bill during their next congress, but said it would deal a significant blow to Democrats. She said the Republicans remain unlikely to block the initiative to repeal the bill from the White House. “We are unlikely to kill it next congress like I believe,” she said in an interview.

The pledge was a contentious move that met with loud applause from Republican National Committee members and many conservatives, one day after the bill was passed in the full Congress. The Washington Post reported Saturday that work on a possible repeal of the law remains under way, but Trump remained committed to restoring Obamacare. In the meantime Trump’s criticism of Obamacare is striking as a combination of the president’s willingness to work hands-on on any efforts to repeal the law and the president’s willingness to work closely with the White House. Trump expressed his praise for Republicans for continuing work on repeal and restoring Obamacare, and he shared the president’s belief that restoring the nation’s economy remains a top priority. He also issued a wide-ranging criticism of current GOP efforts to repeal the Affordable Care Act. Since coming into office last year, Senate Minority Leader Mitch McConnell (R-Ky.) has continued to work with the president in the Senate. While Senate Minority Leader Mitch McConnell (R-Conn.) continues to work in the Senate, House Minority Leader Nancy Pelosi (D-Calif.) and Senate Minority Leader Mitch McConnell (D-Minn.) continue to work in the Senate. In addition, Trump’s brief visit to a conservative fundraising event in North Carolina a week ago surprised many conservatives by noting that he did not immediately visit to a conservative fundraising in North Carolina, where he repealed the law. It is well-known that Trump is no opponent of repealing Obamacare, though he’s been in support of some broader efforts to restore the law. According to analysis by US-based company Verizon, Xbox consoles were down 34 percent in the first quarter of 2013 from the 37 percent drop in 2008. Another possible explanation for these reductions in console sales is the way that games are presented from console to console, or the number of new games being presented in a format that's changed greatly in recent years. Sony's video game services, many of which use mobile devices, is seeing its largest fall in the industry in many years as a result of more people playing video games with a mobile device. Video Game Association data showed the decline in the number of Xbox One-based consoles sold to 9.9 million in the quarter compared to the 13.5 million number a year earlier. But that wasn't the only time the drop has been limited to Xbox One, with an eight percent drop in the total number of Xbox consoles sold to 2.3 million. In the second quarter of 2013, Xbox data also showed a 10 percent drop from the second quarter of 2008 when the total number of Xbox consoles hit 4.2 million. Video game sales have surged as a result of more people using the internet to play video games, with an increased number of people using a mobile device as a buying option. "Competration is slowing a bit, and it is really warming up," Yoshi Koejiya, Sony's chief product officer, told AFP in June. Showtime, one of Sony's top video game services, lets users choose from which genre of video games they should use, and from there, Sony then lets users pick and adjust which version of the genre they prefer. This has led many people to turn off mobile devices at retailers like Showtime and Pricehouse, although experts say they haven't seen much use of these in recent years. Also on the rise is Enix, a service like VideoGamer that lets people use a mobile device to play video games. YouTube isn't far behind, with millions of users using a mobile device while streaming their videos; a service uses a tablet's screen to reveal videos captured in a Showtime stream. Mobile phones are now increasingly dominant in the video game industry, and Sony's success is likely to drive up the price of mobile devices, as consumers now pay more money for viewing online games than by buying a tablet. "There's going to be an increased prize of mobile phones," Paul Hassen, a senior research analyst for Electronica, told AFP in June. Iran backs request for the release of Palestinians held in captivity (West Bank), by AFP JAELBAH, Iran (AFP) - A top Iranian official has said he supports the request for the release of all Palestinians held in the West Bank, calling it a "good start" to the agreement. Iranian Foreign Minister Mohammad Riyadeh said on Friday that the United States had vigorously opposed Israel's request to release the jail mass, calling it a "good start" to the agreement. "The Vice President and the President of the United States have worked very closely together on the issues designated in the Two State Agreement. We have worked very closely together on the issues of reaching an effective and lasting resolution," Mr Riyadeh said at a press conference. "If we hadn't vigorously changed our position on the issue, we would have been ejected. We have worked very closely together with a trusted diplomatic body on reaching an effective resolution." Mr Riyadeh said his country supported asking for the release of Palestinian prisoners in the West Bank as part of a deal that will extend all recaptivity requests to 2010. Israeli Prime Minister Biniq Netanyahu has applauded Israel's request for the release of Palestinian prisoners in the West Bank, saying it was a "good start" to the agreement. "I fully respect Israel. I fully respect the request," Mr Netanyahu said on Friday. "After the negotiations that I have put in place with Israel, I applaude the request. This is good news," he added. Iran's President, Ali Mahmoud Abbas, also said his country supported asking for the release of Palestinian prisoners in the West Bank. "I am very satisfied with the number of Palestinians that were held, and the progress that has been made," Mr Abbas said on Friday. Earlier, in a speech on national television, Mr Abbas said Israel had released over 1,000 Palestinians currently in captivity from jail. Last week, Mr Trump said America was open to releasing Palestinians, and that Israel would not release them. FRANCACO (AP) - California will retain one of its public employees indefinitely, a federal appeals court said Friday, upholding a July 2014 order from a federal judge who upheld a tough crackdown on illegal immigrants. "There will never be a fair debate over a citizen's votes," Judge Paul Erico said Friday, upholding the 43-page ruling. "It would seriously jeopardize our right as a people, to vote." The Third Circuit Court of Appeals issued a ruling to reject a lawsuit from Giuli's father, Michael Giuli. The defendants said Giuli was a former 15-time employee who is not living here illegally or breaking California's immigration laws. They claimed Giuli went to jail in a detention center for assisting unlicensed immigrants and working as a waitress at San Almado Jail. The lawsuit, Giuli's family declined immediately comment, said he worked professionally for the state Department of Justice after receiving his job on the state's Immigrant resilience Program. "That's not a professional job," Giuli told the family. "We need to treat you like a criminal in order to pursue professional careers." The defendants' lawsuit claimed four of them were undocumented immigrants who flew into the state in security or administrative positions. Civil rights groups, many of them, have denied the allegations. Erico said he isn't happy about the court's ruling that Giuli has to be released from jail, but that he's studying the case as it moves forward. Fantas's father, Jasper Robert Fantas, said his son faces 9 months in jail and is prepared to try him. He said the court needed to seal his son's release. Erin White of the California American Civil Liberties Union said the defendants' release was sealed indefinitely because Giuli has been convicted of drug crimes. "This ruling is going to send a clear signal to Californians to comply with (state law) and respect voting rights," White said. Rep. Deencon Garcia, D-Californ, said he welcomed the court's unanimous ruling because there was a constitutional precedent for a judge to retain illegal immigrants in jail who are not living here illegally. "There are far, far too many blue-collar public employees who are allowed to serve as public employees for drug crimes convicted under California law," Garcia said in a statement. "This ruling shines a light on the issue of undocumented immigrants who are living here illegally." MICHALS (WKZ) – A handful of states, including Michigan, Washington, and Massachusetts, already legalized the use of medical marijuana for children with various conditions. Each state voted unanimously Monday to move the legalization forward for the use of medical marijuana, according to the Michigan Department of Public Health. Licenses for medical marijuana will be available in any form for 1-year-olds aged 10 and older beginning Oct. 31, according to the Michigan Department of Public Health and Human Resources. Preview applications are scheduled until Oct. 9, when 1-year-olds aged 12 and older will be able to pick up using the drug starting Oct. 1. The drug will be available for children with various conditions, including Alzheimer’s disease, multiple sclerosis and depression, a spokeswoman said. "As infants, we are uniquely interested in medical marijuana due to its recreational and clinical benefits in treating various conditions," she said. "We share our responsibilities to make Michigan the first state in the country to legalize medical marijuana for infant children." "Like with all advocates supporting this initiative, we want to ensure that children 13 and older can take advantage of the benefits and risks associated with growing this clinically beneficial plant," Dr James Johnson, spokesman specialist at the U.S. Centers for Disease Control and Prevention, said in a statement. A preliminary application for the medical marijuana license will be available to every new child once they complete the new legalization process. They are required to prove their prior experiences using medical marijuana, undergo a medical examination and share their use history with their doctors. If they don’t have government approval, they cannot apply for a new license. They can opt out of using the medical marijuana before Oct. 31 because Michigan has no regulatory agencies. At present, data provided by the Michigan Department of Public Health and Human Resources shows that 50 percent of college graduates regularly use the drug and 25 percent of college graduates use the substance if they had a prior experience using it. Overall, only 28 percent of college graduates are using the drug as adults and 43 percent of college graduates are using it as adults. Nineteen percent will use the substance regularly when they reach age 21, according to U.S. Department of Health data. Oregon opened the way for legalization in May, becoming the first state to legalize medical marijuana for children. In June, New York City became the first city to fully legalize the drug. Health experts and lawmakers think the process is going to begin quickly. "Tomorrow, Michigan is the only state in the country where children early in childhood and adulthood will get a license for medical marijuana in any form," Yvanna Taylor, spokeswoman for the U.S. Center for Disease Control and Prevention, said in a statement. "We’ll have to wait and see the full impact of our state’s initiative." Other states that have already legalized medical marijuana for children include Arizona, Colorado, Nebraska, New Mexico and Texas. Along with moving the legalization forward, the State Department is also intensifying its efforts to include the medical marijuana program into President Obama’s National Security Authorization Program. (AP Photo/Sean Van Heal, AP) WASHINGTON (AP) — Wisconsin lawmakers are expected to act on a bill that would allow more than 90 million people to enter the state without trial. The bill is expected to come into effect after about 11 months of debate. The bill would require 90 million people within the state to cast their ballots, including most undocumented immigrants. The Senate in Wisconsin is scheduled for a statewide vote in November on bills that would violate the constitution and repeal the right to vote entirely. The bill attempts to hinder the state's efforts to prevent provisions of federal laws from allowing undocumented immigrants to be prosecutiond on felony charges, including a life sentence. "We've spent the past two years trying to ensure Wisconsin residents have the right to vote legitimately, fairly and openly," said House Majority Leader Nathan Leahy, a Democrat who is emerging as the favorite to lead the state Senate. "This bill has passed both the House and the Senate in a way that better serves the people of Wisconsin." If unsupported by the Senate, the bill is set to come into effect on Nov. 21, a week before the June general election. It is expected to be approved by the state House of Representatives at some point in the process. If approved, the bill would require the statewide support of the state's Senate. It would also prevent federal laws from allowing about 90 million undocumented immigrants to enter the state, be prosecuted on felony charges, and be charged and deported. Supporters of the bill say the law's provisions, including deferred action, deportations and even a life sentence, could be too targeted at gay undocumented immigrants. Approximately 93 percent of Wisconsin's population is white. More than 54 million are held without trial. White Americans make up 87.4 percent of the state's population. Hispanics account for about 29.4 percent of Wisconsin's population. nationwide, about one-fourth of the state's 77.6 million residents are white. Approximately 60 percent of the state's total residents are 65 years old or older. "Without this bill become law, Wisconsin would be stuck in an era of deferred action and deportations," said Casey Guin, a law professor at Rutgers University. Opponents of the bill argue it could serve as a too broad disciplinary deportation policy. It would include few Senate votes and say it's too targeted at immigrants from other parts of the state. Although the bill is expected to pass the Senate after 11 months of debate, which may become law by then, supporters of the current measure argue it could set a precedent for passage in the future. Deferred action and deportations are aimed at gay undocumented immigrants, while current deportation policies see people held without trial. By the end of the year, 71,515 gay and lesbian men have been held under house arrest in detention centers nationwide, according to an annual report by the Centers for Disease Control. Advocates say Wisconsin's right-to-vo provisions are unconstitutional. They argue they're broad, poorly implemented and are therefore unconstitutional. "When does a resident have right to vote? We haven't considered it," said Beryla Smith, spokeswoman for the Wisconsin Voting Alliance, a group that advocates for non-voting rights in the state. "It's not going to be a token of protection for our residents." Im Smith, a legal adviser to the National Coalition on LGBT Rights, said most states except Wisconsin would not require residents 65 years old or older to cast ballots. The state would require residents to be below 10 years of statutory age in order to cast a ballot. Wisconsin's senate has said it will consider future bills to uphold some of the law's provisions, but it is unlikely to consider any new ones until the general election later this month. (Reuters) -- - FBI Director Robert Mueller, the agent-in-charge of the investigation of Russian interference in the 2016 presidential election, officially resigned late Monday, according to a representative of the subcommittee on National Intelligence. Mueller's resignation " occurred during an ongoing investigation of the FBI's work with National Intelligence and its contacts with foreign intelligences," a press release said. Until Wednesday on Sunday, Mueller's office had not said what triggered the resignation. Mueller's office had not immediately responded to a request for comment on Sunday. Mueller, a close political aide to Hillary Clinton's campaign, made contacts with U.S. intelligence during the course of the investigation that triggered his resignation. In 2015, Mueller began working with Trump campaign manager Corey Bannon and his associates to help the Department of Justice's subcommittee on foreign intelligence investigate allegations of "Russian interfering" that helped Donald Trump eventually win the presidential election. Mueller served as an FBI director from 2013-192015, when he joined the agency as the chairman of the House Intelligence Committee. He was a senior special counsel and served in that position for years before moving on to work as Assistant Director of National Intelligence. Prior to joining the FBI, Mueller also held a position of serving as Assistant Director of National Intelligence for the investigation of Russian interfering during Donald Trump's presidential campaign. Between 2013 and 2015, Mueller began working with Trump campaign manager Corey Bannon and his associates to help the Department of Justice gather information regarding its work with foreign intelligences. Following Mueller's resignation, Bannon presided over a five-month investigation of Russian interference, according to the subcommittee. At the time of Mueller's resignation, he was promoted to director of FBI operations in the ongoing phase of the investigation. Mueller's responsibilities include working in the House Intelligence Committee and the Office of Foreign Agents, according to a subcommittee. U.S. Senator James Comey, D-Mass., who sits on the committee, said during Mueller's resignation that there had been no evidence of Russian interference in the Clinton's campaign. "I have not come across any evidence of Russian interference," Comey said. "I've been working with the FBI on finalizing an investigation, although we have yet to hear any final findings There is no evidence of Russian interference in the success of the Trump campaign." During his resignation, Comey said he had not come across any evidence of Russia helping the Trump campaign. Former Attorney General Michael Flynn, who was FBI director until 2000, said in a statement issued on Sunday that Comey "experienceed lasting pain" as a result of his resignation. "I've been working closely with the FBI on finalizing an investigation, although we have yet to hear any final findings," Flynn said in a statement issued on Sunday. After presided over a five-month investigation of Russian interference in the 2016 election, Flynn emphasized that he saw no doubt that Russia had "an adverse influence" on the 2016 election. He said he wasn't exactly "shocked" at any further Russian interference in the outcome of the 2016 election..

CNET Apple will release a major update that will make it easier for users to share their media with Apple's Apple Watch app, the company said. Getty Images In a rare move meant to keep parents from changing their surnames, the Education Department has added a range of requirements that parents change their surname, as part of a set of new rules announced Monday. The rules, which are still preliminary, require parents to change their surnames no later than three months after their child is born, and are required on all children between ages 14 and 15, according to a statement from the children’s agency. Under the rules, parents who would prefer to have their surname memorized after their child is born will receive additional fees by the current school year, the agency said. A primary difference with the agency’s new rules is that parents who would prefer to change their child surnames must have all of their children’ nicknames memorized within the first six months of their school year, the agency said. That applies especially to children where parents are either unwilling or unwilling to change their surnames, or are unwilling to rename them after the school year. Under the rules, parents must change their surnames after the four-and-a-half year old’s mother has been born, or shortly after the surname has been memorized. “We strongly encourage parents to change 14- and 15-year-olds’ surnames as quickly as they can,” Daniel Weder, spokesman for the National Association of Education for Adolescent Children, said in a statement..

BOSTON, Jan 11, 2017 (Reuters) - Development nations achieved more than nine percentage points in GDP growth in 2010-11 than they had previous years, a United Nations agency said on. Inflows among 10 developing nations increased nine percentage points during the 2010-2011 period, the Organization of Economic Cooperation and Development (UNOECD) said in a report on Wednesday, compared to nine percentage points for the prior period. The total figure the UNOECD said represents a 10 percentage point increase over the prior period. UNOECD said a total of 10 developing nations achieved more than nine percentage points in GDP growth between 2010 and 2012. The most significant, the report said, were China, Japan, North Korea and South Africa during this time period. Inflows among these nations increased by 2.0 and 0.4 percentage points, respectively, with average economic growth down 5.6 percentage points, and average global economic growth up 1.73 percentage points. UNOECD estimated that GDP inflows among developing nations increased 2.86 percentage points between 2010 and 2012, but the agency said data from the time period indicated that GDP growth after 2010-11 was at a relatively slow pace. “Research conducted during this time period indicated that most developing nations’ GDP growth was not affected by changing economic conditions and that developing nations’ GDP inflows were not affected,” the report noted.

Member states will then be allowed to implement carbon pollution reduction in excess of the EU target of 2.95 trillion megawatts per kilowatt by the end of 2040. By 2030, the IEA and Italy will benefit from carbon pollution cuts by as much as 25 percent, 60 percent and 70 percent respectively, the French study said. WASHINGTON (Reuters) - President Barack Obama is pulling military forces out of al Rafqa District in eastern Syria as part of an offensive against ISIS and its allies, U.S. officials said late Wednesday. A gunman takes over the area of the U.S.-led coalition after the coalition liberates Rafqa October 28, 2014. REUTERS/Asiah Ahmad The U.S. Central Command is moving troops to gain possession and control of al Rafqa District, but details have not been released on when military forces will be removed from the district. “For the first time during this administration, President Obama is pulling forces out of al Rafqa District of eastern Syria to protect themselves from ISIS and its allies,” General George Brooks, commander of the U.S. Central Command, said at a briefing late Wednesday in Khadaz. The U.S. military has supplied 15,000 weapons, other supplies and equipment to Rafqa District of eastern Syria since the shelling of ISIS in May. The Washington-led coalition liberated Rafqa, 115 kilometers, west of Syria last month from Islamic militants known as Isis. After the shelling of ISIS, top U.S. Central Command forces reached the area alongside Syrian Army jets. U.S. officials said Obama will pull military forces out of al Rafqa District, a smaller area about 180 kilometers (199 miles) southwest of Syria, as part of the U.S. offensive against Isis, a deadly Islamist group, according to the U.S. Wartime Strategic Report. The military will move into the district to protect itself against Isis and its fighters, the report said. U.S. officials said the offensive will allow ISIS to be able to use its air bases to maintain a stronghold on the area that ISIS fighters say remains disputed. U.S. Central Command and fighter planes were deployed in the offensive against ISIS and its allies in the eastern Syria area as government forces raided on government bases in Syria, killing at least 22 people. Since the offensive began, the military has deployed 20,000 medical units to assist Syrian and government opponents, according to the report. Before the offensive, al Rafqa District was one of the largest districts in eastern Syria. Since the offensive, the military has deployed 20,000 medical units to assist Syrian and government opponents, and some 63,000 military units have been deployed to protect themselves from Isis and its fighters.
